name: Aleksandr Kogan

summary.text: Aleksandr Kogan is a psychology researcher formerly at the University of Cambridge who, through his company Global Science Research (GSR), built the Facebook app known as 'thisisyourdigitallife' (the 'GSRApp'), which collected data from app users and their Facebook friends in 2014 under a contract with SCL. Facebook said in April 2018 that the information of up to 87 million people may have been improperly shared with Cambridge Analytica. Kogan gave evidence to the UK DCMS Committee on 24 April 2018 and to a US Senate Commerce subcommittee on 19 June 2018. In July 2019 he agreed to an FTC administrative order, finalised in December 2019, barring deceptive statements about data collection and requiring deletion of the data.

facts.claim: The FTC's July 2019 complaint describes Kogan's app as the 'GSRApp', also known as the 'thisisyourdigitallife' app, and alleged that Cambridge Analytica, Nix and Kogan deceived consumers by falsely claiming they did not collect personally identifiable information from Facebook users who took survey questions.
facts.quote: The FTC alleged that Cambridge Analytica, Nix, and Kogan deceived consumers by falsely claiming they did not collect any personally identifiable information from Facebook users who took survey questions.

sources.title: FTC Sues Cambridge Analytica, Settles with Former CEO and App Developer

facts.claim: In July 2019 Kogan agreed to a proposed FTC administrative order barring him from making false or deceptive statements about how he collects, uses, shares or sells personal information and requiring him to delete or destroy personal information collected via the GSRApp and related work product; the Commission voted 5-0 to finalise the order, dated 18 December 2019.
facts.quote: The orders bar them from making false or deceptive statements about how they collect, use, share, or sell personal information (they are required to delete or destroy any personal information collected from consumers via the GSRApp and any related work product that originated from the data).

facts.claim: Facebook's 4 April 2018 newsroom post by CTO Mike Schroepfer stated that the Facebook information of up to 87 million people, mostly in the US, may have been improperly shared with Cambridge Analytica.
facts.quote: the post says the Facebook information of up to 87 million people, mostly in the US, may have been improperly shared with Cambridge Analytica.

sources.title: An Update on Our Plans to Restrict Data Access on Facebook

facts.claim: Facebook has said that Kogan harvested the data by creating an app on the network that was downloaded by about 270,000 people, and that through friend permissions the app obtained data on far more people.
facts.quote: Facebook says Mr. Kogan harvested the data by creating an app on the social media network that was downloaded by 270,000 people.

sources.title: Senate panel to call key Cambridge Analytica figure to testify

facts.claim: Kogan gave evidence to the UK DCMS Committee on 24 April 2018; press accounts of the session say his company GSR, not Kogan personally, entered a 2014 agreement with SCL to collect demographic and personality data on individuals in 11 US states, for which he was paid $800,000, and that he said he had deleted the Facebook data and derivatives to the best of his knowledge.
facts.quote: Kogan never signed a contract with Cambridge Analytica himself, but his company, Global Science Research, did enter an agreement with SCL. Under the 2014 agreement, SCL wanted Kogan's company to collect demographic and personality data of individuals in 11 US states. He was paid $800,000 for the job.

facts.claim: Kogan testified on 19 June 2018 before the US Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Consumer Protection, Product Safety, Insurance, and Data Security at a hearing titled 'Cambridge Analytica and Other Facebook Partners: Examining Data Privacy Risks', alongside Ashkan Soltani and John Battelle; he argued that his work had little value for ad targeting because Facebook's ads platform already gave SCL targeting tools.
facts.quote: He argued that the Facebook ads platform already gave SCL tools for targeted advertising, so his project added little.

facts.claim: Kogan publicly disputed Christopher Wylie's Senate Judiciary testimony in May 2018, saying Wylie had 'a very active imagination without actual knowledge to back it up'.
facts.quote: He said Wylie has a very active imagination without actual knowledge to back it up.

openQuestions: Kogan's written Senate statement (commerce.senate.gov) and the DCMS transcript of 24 April 2018 should be checked for his exact wording on the $800,000 payment, the 11 US states and data deletion; those figures are from TechCrunch and SBS accounts of the hearing.

Companies House records show a director named 'Aleksandr Spectre' appointed to GSR in September 2015; press accounts describe Kogan as having used the surname Spectre, which was not confirmed from a primary record here.
Kogan's 2019 defamation suit against Facebook (reported by Euronews/NBC) was not researched.
